signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Tokyo CPI Repricing
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 109.467 as the G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers a 1.954% leader-to-laggard divergence over the 1W window. JPY leads the G10 complex with a 1W average gain of +1.109% across 7 pairs following the hotter-than-forecast Tokyo Core CPI print of 2.7% year-over-year against 1.9% expected. AUD lags the entire G10 board with a 1W average decline of -0.845% across 4 pairs, despite RBA at 4.6% vs BoJ 1.25% offering a +335bp nominal carry advantage and AONIA 4.60% vs TONA 1.23% giving a +337bp OIS spread. JPY COT Leveraged Funds positioning sits at net long +4,472 contracts (pctl 98, z +2.66), indicating stretched speculative long positioning in the yen even as Tokyo rate volatility accelerates. With AUD/USD below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6933, the massive carry premium in AUD/JPY is failing to insulate the cross against JPY strength. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY; yen macro repricing overrides the +335bp carry buffer. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting on 30 Oct — hold priced. Risk: JPY Leveraged Funds long unwind from 98th percentile relieves cross pressure.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + CPI Driver
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 157.78, holding below its SMA50 at 158.15 and SMA200 at 158.48 while remaining above the SMA20 at 156.18. Saxo Bank 25d Risk Reversals trade at an extreme -2.60 put skew, reflecting substantial options market demand for downside protection despite a +275bp Fed-BoJ policy rate spread (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) and a +267bp SOFR-TONA carry advantage. JPY COT Leveraged Funds positioning shows a crowded long profile at net +4,472 contracts with a 52-week percentile of 98 (z +2.66), even after a WoW reduction of 15,597 contracts. Spot is under pressure following the Tokyo Core CPI upside surprise of 2.7% versus 1.9% consensus, which reinforces policy tightening expectations in Tokyo. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; extreme put skew and domestic inflation support JPY over the USD carry gap. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 12:30 UTC — forecast 52K. Risk: A sharp US jobs beat sends US 2Y yields higher, expanding the 295bp US-JP 2Y yield advantage and forcing put coverage.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Rate Divergence + Retail Positioning Skew
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1263, trapped in a deterministic downtrend below its SMA20 (1.1482), SMA50 (1.1532), and SMA200 (1.1615). Fed 4.00% (hiking) vs ECB 2.65% (hiking) provides a +135bp carry advantage favoring the dollar, reinforced by SOFR 3.90% vs ESTR 2.44% delivering a +146bp OIS differential. The 2Y yield spread between Germany and the US sits at -182bp, having widened by 43bp over the last 5 sessions in the dollar's favor. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net short EUR at -58,805 contracts (WoW -7,450), while retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data is positioned 87% long versus 13% short. This clear divergence between institutional accumulation of shorts and extreme retail contrarian longs highlights capitulation risk for retail longs if support fails. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent rate spread widening and retail overhang keep rallies capped. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI y/y at 09:00 UTC — forecast 3.0%. Risk: Eurozone core inflation beats significantly, forcing an ECB hawkish pivot and closing the rate spread.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real-Yield Drag
signals.text: GBP/USD changes hands at 1.3217, trading beneath its SMA20 (1.3383), SMA50 (1.3455), and SMA200 (1.3447). Saxo Bank options analytics report 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.6% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.2%, establishing an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.4% that points to heavy downside hedging demand. The rate backdrop is unfavorable for sterling, with BoE at 3.75% on hold vs Fed 4.00% hiking (+25bp spread favoring USD) and the UK-US 2Y yield spread shifting 31bp in the dollar's favor over the past 5 sessions to -24bp. FRED yield decomposition shows US 5Y nominal yields rose 23bp over 5 days (as of Sep 29), led almost entirely by real yields rising 21bp with breakevens adding only 2bp. Furthermore, GBP speculative positioning shows Leveraged Funds shedding 12,179 contracts WoW to +6,519 net (pctl 8, z -1.66), reflecting aggressive long liquidation. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; elevated options hedging and real yield pressure keep downside open toward 1.3150. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 12:30 UTC — forecast 52K. Risk: US average hourly earnings miss sharply, triggering a broad USD pullback across G10.
